stem_bark.text: The bark of Butea monosperma is greyish or pale brown-coloured, longitudinally fissured and transversally cracked.
stem_bark.text_html: The bark of Butea monosperma is greyish or pale brown-coloured, longitudinally fissured and transversally cracked.

seed.text: The seed of Butea monosperma is compressed, ellipsoid and brownish-coloured. The seed is 3-3.5 cm long and 2-2.5 cm wide. There is only one seed per pod.
seed.text_html: The seed of Butea monosperma is compressed, ellipsoid and brownish-coloured. The seed is 3-3.5 cm long and 2-2.5 cm wide. There is only one seed per pod.

fruit.text: The fruit of Butea monosperma is a flattened pod . It is velvety, 12-15 cm long and 5-6 cm wide and light brown-coloured. Each pod contains only one seed.
fruit.text_html: The fruit of Butea monosperma is a flattened pod. It is velvety, 12-15 cm long and 5-6 cm wide and light brown-coloured. Each pod contains only one seed.

flower.text: The flowers of Butea monosperma are grouped in axillary racemes (up to 40 cm long) on leafless branchlets. The flowers have a 3-4 cm long peduncle . The flowers are 5-merous. The calyx-tube is campanulate, 5-lobed and 2 cm long and 1.5 cm across. The calyx is green and finely pubescent. The corolla is composed of 5 bright orange-coloured and pubescent petals. The corolla is about 4-5 cm across. The androecium is composed of a curved and 5-6 cm long staminal sheath with 9 free stamens (1.5-2 cm long) at the end. 1 stamen is completely free. The pistil is composed of a curved and 4-4.5 cm long style and a simple stigma . The ovary is oblong and about 2.5 cm long. The buds are covered with short hairs (velvety). The flowers are fragrant.
flower.text_html:
The flowers of Butea monosperma are grouped in axillary racemes (up to 40 cm long) on leafless branchlets.
The flowers have a 3-4 cm long peduncle.
The flowers are 5-merous.
The calyx-tube is campanulate, 5-lobed and 2 cm long and 1.5 cm across. The calyx is green and finely pubescent.
The corolla is composed of 5 bright orange-coloured and pubescent petals. The corolla is about 4-5 cm across.
The androecium is composed of a curved and 5-6 cm long staminal sheath with 9 free stamens (1.5-2 cm long) at the end. 1 stamen is completely free.
The pistil is composed of a curved and 4-4.5 cm long style and a simple stigma.
The ovary is oblong and about 2.5 cm long.
The buds are covered with short hairs (velvety).
The flowers are fragrant.

leaf.text: The leaves of Butea monosperma grow alternately on the stem (spirally arranged). The leaf is compound, trifoliate. The leaflets are dark green-coloured above and paler beneath. The leaf is coriaceous and pubescent on both sides. The leaflets have a 0.8-1 cm long petiole . The leaflet of Butea monosperma is 8-12 cm long and 6-8 cm wide. The shape of the blade is ovate, the apex is acute, the base is cuneate or oblique and the margins are entire. The venation of the leaf is reticulate with a prominent midrib.

habit.text: Butea monosperma is a medium-sized and deciduous tree growing up to 10-12 m high.

ecology.text: Butea monosperma is "found throughout the drier parts of India, often gregarious in forests, open grasslands and wastelands. A characteristic tree of the plains, it often forms pure patches in grazing grounds and other open places". ( Orwa C., Mutua A., Kindt R., Jamnadass R., Anthony S., 2009, Agroforestree Database: a tree reference and selection guide )

distribution.text: Indian subcontinent, Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Indonesia.
distribution.text_html:
• Distribution :

    Indian subcontinent, Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Indonesia.

reproduction_dispersal.text: Butea monosperma is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures). Butea monosperma is mainly pollinated by birds. Mechanical dispersal : barochory (dispersal of seeds by gravity), self-propagation. The seeds disperse from the pods and germinate on sites with favourable conditions : the ripe dry fruits burst and scatter the seeds.
reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :

    Butea monosperma is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures).

  • Mode of pollination :

    Butea monosperma is mainly pollinated by birds.

  • Seed dispersal :

    Mechanical dispersal : barochory (dispersal of seeds by gravity), self-propagation.
    The seeds disperse from the pods and germinate on sites with favourable conditions : the ripe dry fruits burst and scatter the seeds.

others.text: In India, the tree is an important host for the lac insect ( Laccifer lacca ), which produces shellac. Source : Orwa C., Mutua A., Kindt R., Jamnadass R., Anthony S., 2009, Agroforestree Database: a tree reference and selection guide

veterinary.text: The young leaves of Butea monosperma are a good fodder .

handicrafts.text: A fibre is obtained from the inner bark. It is used for cordage, caulking the seams of boats and making paper. A red exudate is obtained from the bark, hardening into a gum known as "butea gum" or "Bengal kino". It is used as a dye and as tannin . A bright yellow to deep orange-red dye , known as butein , prepared from the flowers is used especially for dyeing silk and sometimes for cotton. This dye is used by Hindus to mark the forehead. Source : Orwa C., Mutua A., Kindt R., Jamnadass R., Anthony S., 2009, Agroforestree Database: a tree reference and selection guide

medicinal.text: The flowers of Butea monosperma are useful in the treatment of liver disorders. The seeds are anthelmintic. The gum is a powerful astringent and it is applied in cases of diarrhoea. Source : Orwa C., Mutua A., Kindt R., Jamnadass R., Anthony S., 2009, Agroforestree Database: a tree reference and selection guide

reforestation.text: Butea monosperma is able to flourish in a wide range of soils. It thrives in open areas. The species is propagated by seeds. 12 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :

    Butea monosperma is able to flourish in a wide range of soils. It thrives in open areas.
    The species is propagated by seeds.

  • Seed treatments :

    12 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
